title: Enforce protected main and environment gates
question: Which GitHub plan/publicity and solo-owner review policy should enforce protected main, required checks, sensitive-path ownership and environment approvals without deadlocking delivery?
evidence: The private repository has no branch protection, rulesets or GitHub Environments.
GitHub rulesets and classic branch protection APIs both return HTTP 403 requiring GitHub Pro or a public repository.
Only one authorised Product Authority/repository owner is currently configured, so mandatory independent approval would deadlock delivery until a second reviewer exists.
The Product Authority selected Option B and changed the repository visibility to public on 29 August 2026.
Public visibility enabled classic main-branch protection with strict required Phase 1 checks, pull requests, linear history, resolved conversations and administrator enforcement.

options.description: Keep private and upgrade to a protection-capable plan; require PR/checks now and enable one approval when a second authorised reviewer exists.
Make the repository public and configure protection.
Remain private on the current plan with procedural controls only.
impacts: Direct pushes and ungated environment actions cannot be mechanically prevented

recommendation.reason: It best preserves the current private posture while enabling enforceable CI, branch and environment controls; a zero-approval solo-owner phase avoids deadlock until a second authorised reviewer exists.

decision: Make the repository public and configure enforceable remote protection. Require zero approving reviews while there is one authorised reviewer; move to one independent approval and required CODEOWNER review when a second authorised reviewer exists.
blockedScope: GitHub Environment approval gates remain unwired until deployment workflows and least-privilege identities are ready
continuingWork: Synthetic local/dev work inside DEC-041 and DEC-054
